transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendes (Nova AI CTO), Aisha Khan (ML Eng), Lydia Park (Infra), Tom W. (Product)
notes_and_summary: Summary: Nova AI is evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private for a customer-facing summarization/assistant product. Primary constraints: p95 latency <= 300ms for short prompts ( <= 128 tokens), burst concurrency up to 150 simultaneous streams, sustained throughput goal ~18k tokens/sec aggregate. They want to run token/sec benchmarks and see tradeoffs for batching/quantization and streaming behavior. Security/regulatory concerns may push them to Private (VPC) for EU data residency.
full_transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE. Priya our solutions engineer is here. Quick intros?
[00:08] Carlos: Hey, Carlos here, CTO at Nova AI, we build a summarization assistant used by enterprise customers, lots of short prompts and some longer documents.
[00:15] Aisha: Hi, Aisha on ML, I'll own the evaluation work. Lydia: Lydia on infra.
[00:22] Jordan: Great. Today we want to understand your latency/throughput goals, concurrency, and whether hosted/dedicated/private makes sense. Priya will dig into perf.
[00:32] Priya: Quick note - transcription may flip some product names, but when I say Redwood Dedicated I mean our reserved GPU pools. Also we can do streaming and function-style responses.
[00:45] Tom: Our SLA target is p95 under 300ms for the short-turn queries (prompt+context ~ 100 tokens). For longer docs it's okay to be higher, like 800-1200ms.
[00:55] Priya: Good, is that p95 end-to-end including network from customer region?
[01:02] Carlos: We're counting from our backend to the Redwood endpoint to response complete, yes. We run in GCP europe-west1.
[01:10] Priya: Okay, that affects routing. For hosted we can place endpoints in eu-west. For Dedicated you get reserved capacity in region. Private (VPC) adds network overhead but reduces cross-tenant variance.
[01:25] Lydia: We're also concerned about streaming for partial tokens - real-time UI uses streaming partial responses. How does that affect p95?
[01:32] Priya: Streaming usually increases perceived latency since first token latency is what matters for UX. We can optimize for first-token p95 and then sustain throughput for token/sec. We typically tune batch windows to not hurt first token beyond target.
[01:46] Aisha: Our peak concurrency is expected to be 120-150 short requests concurrently during workday spikes, plus occasional longer document batches of 10 concurrent long jobs.
[01:56] Priya: For concurrency that high, Dedicated with autoscaling or our Hosted with burst capacity are both options. Dedicated gives predictable throughput; hosted can be cheaper if you can tolerate fallbacks.
[02:08] Jordan: Can you share typical request/response size and tokens per request?
[02:12] Aisha: Typical short QA is 80-120 tokens input, response 40-80 tokens. Long jobs range 2k-8k tokens.
[02:20] Priya: That maps to tokens/sec targets - you said aggregate 18k tokens/sec?
[02:24] Carlos: Yeah peak around 15-20k tokens/sec, sustained 8-10k.
[02:29] Priya: Good. For p95 under 300ms for short flows we recommend a low-batch, low-latency config: smaller batch sizes, favor kernels for short sequence lengths and potentially int8 quantization if model supports it. We can provide expected p95 numbers per model variant.
[02:46] Tom: What about token/sec benchmarks — how do you run them?
[02:50] Priya: We provide a benchmark harness template — you supply a representative prompt set and concurrency pattern, we run token/sec and tail latency tests. We also provide profiling: per-token latency, KV cache hit rates, batching stats.
[03:05] Jordan: For Dedicated, we can commit reserved capacity. That gets you consistent p95s and throughput, but there's a cost tradeoff vs hosted per-token.
[03:14] Carlos: Any example numbers you can share now? Rough ballpark for p95 with a 7B-ish open model?
[03:20] Priya: Rough - hosted, eu region, streaming first-token p95 for short prompts on a tuned 7B quantized model might be ~200-350ms (with variance). Dedicated, same model on reserved A100-equivalent, we often see 120-220ms p95. But these are noisy numbers; exact depends on kernel selection, batch mix, and vseq length.
[03:41] Aisha: Does KV cache help for follow ups?
[03:44] Priya: Yes, prefix/KV caching cuts repeated context compute dramatically. For chat-style sequences where many tokens are repeated, p95 for follow-ups drops by 30-60% depending on cache hit.
[03:56] Lydia: Network egress and VPC setup — Private/VPC option, does that push latency up?
[04:01] Priya: Private deployments add one hop — customer-managed network and reverse-proxy. Usually adds 20-60ms depending on infra. But you get stronger isolation and control over residency.
[04:14] Jordan: Security checklist - they asked about SOC 2, SAML/SSO, KMS/HSM, audit logs. We have SOC2, SSO via SAML/SCIM, KMS integrations, and detailed audit logs we can share.
[04:27] Carlos: We'll need SOC2 and data residency docs before a pilot. Also encryption at rest with customer-managed keys is a must.
[04:35] Priya: We'll attach our compliance pack. For Private we can support CMKs and HSM integrations.
[04:42] Jordan: Back to perf — what's the typical batch window you tune?
[04:46] Priya: We dynamically tune, but for low-latency configs we use <10ms batch windows and small max batch sizes to avoid increasing p95. For throughput optimized configs we increase batch windows to 20-50ms and larger batch sizes.
[04:58] Aisha: Quantization impact — does int8 hurt quality?
[05:01] Priya: There's a small quality delta; we run evaluations on your eval set. Redwood Optimize will suggest quantization profiles per workload (int8 / int4 options depending on model).
[05:11] Carlos: For throughput tests, we want to know tokens/sec per GPU and how many GPUs we'd need for 20k tokens/sec sustained.
[05:18] Priya: Depends on model and quantization. As an example, tuned 7B int8 on an A100-equivalent may do ~6k-8k tokens/sec per GPU for medium-length tokens. 20k sustained might need 3-4 GPUs with appropriate batching. We'll validate with your prompts.
[05:34] Tom: How do you handle graceful degradation if capacity is constrained?
[05:38] Jordan: Our smart routing can fallback to compatible model variants or lower-precision variants, and we can route by cost/latency tiers and region. You can set automatic fallback policies.
[05:49] Aisha: For the smoke test we want to run: 1) first-token p95 for short prompts under concurrency 150, 2) sustained token/sec run for 30 minutes at 10k and burst to 20k, 3) streaming consistency check.
[06:05] Priya: That's a good test plan. We'll need representative prompts and an account for the harness. Also what metrics do you want logged? latency percentiles, tokens/sec, batch sizes, KV hits, error rates?
[06:17] Lydia: All of the above plus network RTT from our VPC.
[06:21] Jordan: Pricing note — hosted is per-token + optional burst plan. Dedicated is reserved monthly with an estimate based on committed GPUs. We'll share pricing bands in the follow-up.
[06:32] Carlos: Competitors — we've been talking to Anthropic and considering a managed Anthropic offering for latency. How do you compare?
[06:40] Priya: We focus on production controls and predictable economics and give more deployment flexibility (dedicated/private). We also expose detailed per-route latency/cost breakdowns so you can tune.
[06:50] Tom: Any gotchas for multi-region?
[06:53] Priya: Cross-region replication and routing add complexity; it's usually fine but increase egress and routing latencies. You can pin endpoints to region for lowest latency.
[07:03] Jordan: Let's talk scheduling. We can run an initial bench next week. We'll need the prompt set and concurrency script by Friday.
[07:10] Carlos: We'll aim to provide prompts and a 2-hour window to run tests. Also we need baseline numbers for our current infra (we'll share internal metrics).
[07:16] Priya: For the bench, please include: list of prompts, expected token lengths, concurrency pattern (ramp up/down), and whether to simulate streaming.
[07:26] Aisha: On the longer docs — tokenization and chunking behavior interplay with KV cache; if many docs reuse context we can leverage cache to reduce compute.
[07:35] Priya: Correct. For multi-turn conversations we often see 2-3x effective throughput gain from caching.
[07:41] Jordan: Quick practical: we'll propose two configurations in the follow-up — low-latency hosted config and Dedicated reserved pool config with numbers. Priya will include expected p95s and GPU counts.
[07:53] Carlos: Sounds good. Regarding data residency, if we go private we'll need air-gapped option for specific EU customers. Is that supported?
[08:00] Priya: Yes, private/on-prem packages are an option; support and install can be provided under enterprise contract. Lead times are longer.
[08:08] Tom: Anything else about instrumentation?
[08:10] Priya: We instrument token-level sampling, and have dashboards for per-route p50/p95/p99, batch sizes, KV cache stats, and cost per token. You can hook up tracing for end-to-end observability.
[08:22] Jordan: Ok let's recap next steps. Carlos: provide prompts and concurrency spec. Jordan/Priya: share benchmark harness, pricing, SOC2 + data residency docs, proposal for Dedicated config. Schedule bench next Tue.
[08:36] Carlos: Good. Thanks everyone.
[08:40] Jordan: Thanks all. We'll follow up in email with artifacts.
[08:44] END
notes: Transcript contains occasional transcription artifacts, speaker labels approximated. Benchmarks and numeric examples are approximate and subject to validation by Redwood SE during tests.
